properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued August 2 at 3:30PM EDT until August 3 at 9:00PM EDT by NWS Upton NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 9 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Kings (Brooklyn), Southwest Suffolk, Southeast
Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...From 6 AM to 9 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Life-threatening rip currents are
likely for all people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting
the beaches should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can
sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

If you enter the surf zone, always have a flotation device with
you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions expected with highs 80 to 90 degrees above
8000 feet and 90 to 100 degrees below 8000 feet. This will result
in Moderate Heat Risk.

* WHERE...In California, Eastern Sierra Slopes and White Mountains of
Inyo County. In Nevada, Sheep Range and Spring Mountains-Red Rock
Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 2 at 12:12PM MST until August 4 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot and humid conditions. Afternoon temperatures
107 to 118. Major to Extreme Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Mostly rural areas of Maricopa County and Northern Pinal
County.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Increase in heat related illnesses, including heat
cramps, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke. Heat stroke can lead to
death.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, Call 2-1-1 to find a free
cooling center, transportation, water and more.
https://www.maricopa.gov/heat
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued August 2 at 12:08PM PDT until August 4 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Medford has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from 2 PM Monday to 9 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Oregon, Fire Weather zones 620, 621, 622, and
623, including Medford, Grants Pass, Ashland, Cave Junction,
Eagle Point, Shady Cove, and the Siskiyous and southern Oregon
Cascades.

* WIND...Northwest 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 25 mph in the
afternoons, becoming east to northeast overnight.

* HUMIDITY...Minimum humidity 8 to 15 percent, with poor
recoveries as low as 20 percent.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Follow all fire restrictions. You can find your county's
emergency sign up form as well as links to fire restrictions at
weather.gov/medford/wildfire. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Be sure you're signed up for your county's emergency alert
system. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan and make
sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for
more information.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions
that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 2 at 12:04PM PDT until August 5 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot daytime conditions with high temperatures between 102
and 110 common. Warm overnight conditions will bring less relief
than usual.

* WHERE...Antelope Valley and nearby foothills.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...There is a high risk for dangerous heat illness,
especially for sensitive groups like the very young, the very old,
those without air conditioning, and those active outdoors.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

If you do not have air conditioning in your home or lack shelter, you
can call 211 for assistance locating appropriate shelter from the
heat.

...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 11 AM MDT /NOON CDT/ TO 8 PM MDT

NORTH DAKOTA...

...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM CDT /7 PM MDT/ THIS

MCKENZIE COUNTIES...

...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM MDT MONDAY DUE TO

...

.Critical fire weather conditions are expected today through Monday
for portions of western and south central North Dakota. A cold front
will shift winds to the west northwest today, and remain breezy.
Meanwhile, dry conditions will bring low afternoon humidity values in
the teens. Thus a Red Flag Warning remains for much of western North
Dakota through this evening. Some western areas will see poor
humidity recoveries tonight, followed by more critical fire weather
conditions with very low humidity values and breezy winds on Monday.
These critical fire weather conditions will also extend into south
central portions of the state. Thus some of the ongoing Red Flag
Warning has been extended, with a new Red Flag Warning issued for the
mentioned south central portions.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of western and southwest North Dakota.

* TIMING...Until 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/ Monday.

* WINDS...North winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity as low as 10 percent today
and as low as 20 percent on Monday.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute to
extreme fire behavior.

Warning.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of central and north central South Dakota.

* TIMING...From noon CDT /11 AM MDT/ to 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/ Monday.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 25 to 35 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

* WHEN...Until 745 PM EDT /645 PM CDT/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying

continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.
Expect many areas of slow moving or standing water.

7 inches of rain have fallen today. Some additional rainfall

Nixon, Youngstown, Cairo, Chipola Park, Majette, Frink,
Saunders, Bayou George, Camp Flowers, Fountain, Bennett,
Scotts Ferry, Singer Road and College Station.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued August 3 at 3:40AM ChST until August 8 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet and dangerous rip
currents expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...North and east facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 PM ChST Saturday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Long-period east to northeast swell, emanating
from distant Typhoon Dolphin, continues to produce a high risk of
rip currents along north and east-facing reefs, along with
hazardous surf along said reefs. As Dolphin continues to move
toward Iwo To, the long-period swell direction is expected to shift
north over the next few days, and then northwest around midweek. As
it does so, a high risk of rip currents and hazardous surf are
expected to develop along west facing reefs later this week.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

If caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline.
If unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 2 at 11:11AM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID
properties.description:
AQAPIH

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due
to wildfire smoke.
Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy.

* WHERE...BANNOCK, BINGHAM, CARIBOU, ONEIDA AND POWER COUNTIES.

* WHEN...THROUGH TUESDAY, AUGUST 4TH.

* IMPACTS...Some members of the general public may experience
health effects; members of sensitive groups may experience more
serious health effects.
properties.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

THIS STATEMENT IS ISSUED BY THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY, AIR QUALITY GROUP. FOR MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT DEQ's
Pocatello Regional Office at (208)236-6160.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning

heat stroke.

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 2 at 8:24AM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air
Quality Advisory for eastern Clackamas County, which is IN EFFECT
UNTIL NOON PDT MONDAY.

An Air Quality Advisory for Smoke has been issued. Wildfires burning
in the region combined with forecasted conditions will cause air
quality to reach unhealthy levels at times through noon PDT Monday.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems. Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

More information about air quality can be found at:
www.oregon.gov/DEQ
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

AQAMT

The Montana Department of Environmental Quality has issued an air
quality alert for Chouteau, Flathead, Glacier, Hill, Lake, Liberty,
Lincoln, Pondera, Sanders, Teton, Toole counties in effect until 9AM
on 08/03/2026
An Air Quality Alert means that particulates have been trending
upwards and that an exceedance of the 24 hour National Ambient Air
Quality Standard (NAAQS) has occurred or may occur in the near
future.

Elevated particulate levels from wildfire smoke

As of 7AM on 08/02/2026, particulate levels in Libby are Unhealthy
for Sensitive Groups.

As of 7AM on 08/02/2026, particulate levels in Billings, Butte, Cut
Bank, Dillon, Frenchtown, Great Falls, Hamilton, Havre, Helena,
Lewistown, Malta, Missoula and Sleeping Giant are Moderate.

When air quality is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups... State and local
health officials recommend that people with respiratory or heart
disease, the elderly and children should limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Moderate... State and local health officials
recommend that unusually sensitive people should consider reducing
prolonged or heavy exertion.

For more information visit the Montana Department of Environmental
Quality at http://todaysair.mtdeq.us

properties.areaDesc: McMullen, TX
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 2 at 8:25AM CDT until August 6 at 4:04AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 19.1 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early
Wednesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.1
feet on 09/22/2018.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Valley West; Kuskokwim Valley East; Lime Village; Interior Kuskokwim Delta; Western Capes; Northern Alaska Peninsula; Bristol Bay Borough (Naknek and King Salmon); Northern Bristol Bay Coast; Inland Bristol Bay; Lake Iliamna / Nila Vena / Nanvarpak
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 2 at 5:05AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
A system moving in from the Bering Sea this morning will bring
widespread, prolonged rainfall for Southwest Alaska through at
least Tuesday. By Tuesday afternoon, widespread rainfall amounts
of 1 to 2 inches are expected across most of Southwest Alaska with
locally higher amounts, up to 2.5 inches possible in the Togiak
area, along the Kuskokwim Valley, and near the western Alaska
Range. Heaviest rainfall will be Sunday night into Monday for the
Kuskokwim Delta and western Bristol Bay and Monday into Tuesday
farther inland, along the western Alaska Range.

For coastal areas of the Western Capes and western Bristol Bay
(Goodnews Bay, Platinum and Togiak), southerly winds of 25 to 35
mph (sustained) will persist Sunday evening through Monday
afternoon. This could bring water levels up to 1 to 2 feet above
the mean high tide line. Winds will be strongest early Monday
morning.

Check the forecast for the latest updates, if you plan to be
outdoors.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 1 at 10:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Saturday August 01 to 400 PM Sunday August 02

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Hot and sunny weather with light winds will
allow ozone to reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category
on Saturday and Sunday. Elevated levels of ozone are possible
throughout the northern Front Range region, with the highest
concentrations most likely in the western portions of the Front
Range.   For Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts, and
advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Sunday, August 2, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: OZONE ACTION DAY ALERT FROM 400 PM SATURDAY UNTIL 400 PM SUNDAY

properties.areaDesc: Adams, CO; Arapahoe, CO; Weld, CO; Larimer, CO; Boulder, CO; Jefferson, CO; Broomfield, CO; Denver, CO; Douglas, CO
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 1 at 6:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Saturday August 01 to 400 PM Sunday August 02

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Hot and sunny weather with light winds will
allow ozone to reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category
on Saturday and Sunday. Elevated levels of ozone are possible
throughout the northern Front Range region, with the highest
concentrations most likely in the western portions of the Front
Range.   For Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts, and
advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Sunday, August 2, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Broomfield, CO; Jefferson, CO; Adams, CO; Denver, CO; Larimer, CO; Douglas, CO; Boulder, CO; Arapahoe, CO; Weld, CO
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 1 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Saturday August 01 to 400 PM Sunday August 02

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Hot and sunny weather with light winds will
allow ozone to reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category
on Saturday and Sunday. Elevated levels of ozone are possible
throughout the northern Front Range region, with the highest
concentrations most likely in the western portions of the Front
Range.   For Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts, and
advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Sunday, August 2, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: OZONE ACTION DAY ALERT FROM 400 PM SATURDAY UNTIL 400 PM SUNDAY

properties.description:
As a coastal system moves across Western Alaska Sunday into
Monday, elevated water levels, widespread rain, and southerly
winds are expected across the area. Water levels could rise 1 to
3 feet above the mean high tide line in coastal areas of the
Bering and Chukchi Seas. Rain totals from Sunday afternoon
through early Tuesday morning are expected to range from 1 to 2
inches south of the Bering Strait and from 0.5 to 1 inch north of
the Bering Strait. From Sunday afternoon through Tuesday night,
southerly winds could gust to 30 to 40 mph, with gusts over 40 mph
possible over the YK Delta. Those in coastal areas should take
extra precautions to ensure that belongings are properly secured
ahead of these increasing winds and water levels.

* WHERE...Clearwater and Idaho Counties.

* WHEN...Until noon PDT August 3, 2026.

* IMPACTS...Members of sensitive groups may experience health
effects. The general public is less likely to be affected.

quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

properties.description:
AQAHGX

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued an
Ozone Action Day for the Houston, Galveston, and Brazoria area for
Sunday, August 2, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone pollution in the Houston, Galveston, and
surrounding areas on Sunday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by
sharing a ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive through lanes, conserving energy and keeping your vehicle
properly tuned.

EPA AirNow: www.airnow.gov/?city=Houston&state=TX&country=USA

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 1 at 11:27AM MST until August 3 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions, with temperatures around 108 to
115 degrees expected below 4000 feet.

* WHERE...Northern Gila and Yavapai counties below 4000 feet;
including the Verde Valley and Black Canyon City.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

Ferry, Okanogan, Pend Oreille, and Stevens Counties until further
notice due to current and expected wildfire smoke from regional
fires. Extremely critical fire weather Saturday will produce
significant smoke from ongoing and emerging fires. Particulate matter

British Columbia.

from ongoing and emerging fires. Shifting winds will likely bring
smoke into these counties beginning Saturday evening. PM2.5 may reach
unhealthy levels.

for cleaner indoor air.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 30 at 4:02PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of ozone pollution. Visit
https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted air
quality levels.

* WHERE...Glendora, San Fernando Valley, Santa Clarita Valley, San
Gabriel Valley, San Bernardino, Redlands, Riverside, Crestline and
the Coachella Valley.. Levels of ozone pollution can vary by time
and location depending on emissions and air pollution transport.

* WHEN...until 8 PM Sunday. The highest ozone levels typically occur
in the afternoon and early-evening hours.

* IMPACTS... Ozone air pollution can cause serious health problems,
including trouble breathing, asthma attacks, and lung damage.
Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with
lung disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, and grilling

To help minimize outdoor ozone air pollution levels:

* Limit the use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment
until evening hours

properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of ozone pollution. Visit
https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted air
quality levels.

* WHERE...San Bernardino, Redlands, Riverside, Crestline and the
Coachella Valley.. Levels of ozone pollution can vary by time and
location depending on emissions and air pollution transport.

* WHEN...until 8 PM Sunday. The highest ozone levels typically occur
in the afternoon and early-evening hours.

* IMPACTS... Ozone air pollution can cause serious health problems,
including trouble breathing, asthma attacks, and lung damage.
Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with
lung disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, and grilling

To help minimize outdoor ozone air pollution levels:

* Limit the use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment
until evening hours
* Try to delay trips to the gas station and the use of household
chemicals until the evening
